reviews.title: I want to rate this highly but
reviews.text: The problem is… Thomas Jones’ voice is on a VAST number of the stories.  More than any other by far, it seems. And that would be fine except the reason there need to be voice options is because not every voice works for everyone.  Unfortunately, his voice (though I adore a British accent) does the opposite of soothe my mind so I can drift to sleep.  There just are way too many that are his voice and not enough cool stories that I’d want to choose that are other voices.  (update:  Still just frustrated that every time a cool sounding story pops up, inevitably when you open it , the narrator is Thomas Jones.  Please for the love have other people voice some of his!! At LEAST give other options. It is so crazy.)

reviews.title: Lots of stories
reviews.text:
My favorite story involves something I typically get excited about. In daily life, I’ll go to a yarn store and bounce with excitement looking at all the tools, skeins of yarn, and potential projects. I was torn when I saw Slumber had an episode where someone spends a day in a Knitting Shop. There’s no way, I thought, to get sleep from something so exciting. 
I know someone walks into the shop. I remember something about different kinds of yarn. That’s it. I’m always asleep before I reach the end. I don’t know how Slumber did it. It’s NOT boring. It’s…pleasant. It’s nice. And I can’t stay awake. To be fair, I haven’t tried. I think it stimulates my excitement in a way where I start to dream about the possibilities but does not make me want to get up to start crafting. 
The result is a clear mind the next day. My energy has picked up and I don’t struggle to get out of bed as much.

reviews.title: Variety is fantastic
reviews.text:
Slumber is truly a blessing for someone with horrible sleep issues as myself.  Winding down for sleep I would select a story to hopefully fall asleep to.  It was like someone was reading a night time story to me again like when I was a little girl!  Some of the artist voices were so soothing that I fell asleep quickly.  I don’t normally take the time to write reviews but Slumber has indeed helped me with my sleep. Unfortunately, I’ve had to cancel my subscription for reasons that I wish I didn’t have to. I will truly miss the stories, and their customer service support (I’m a bit of a neophyte on apps ) but they walked me through it all with the highest respect.  This is all the truth.  Best to Slumber and to whomever is reading this review.
Betty

reviews.title: Replaces intrusive, negative thoughts with stories, music and sounds
reviews.text:
I have PTSD and going to sleep has been a nightmare for me for years. I take different sleep aids through the week in hopes I’ll pass out before my mind spirals. I tried this app expecting it to be more annoying than relaxing, but it was actually nice. 

This app has many genres to choose from like sleep meditations, imaginative stories, classic books and tales, sleepy histories, and more. It even has a genre of stories with no plot for the nights when I’m very mentally active. The lack of a plot lets my mind create imagery without any longing to learn what happens next. 

I love that I can control the volume of the voice, music and sound independently. You can have a track loop and repeat or have the music and white noise continue on as long as you like. I recommend earbuds that are designed for sleeping/lying down if you don’t have speakers or have a partner in bed. 

I’m not as scared to go to bed anymore and it’s only been 2 weeks after 16 years of debilitating sleep stress. So thank you to all involved in making this app and all the options available to fit any mood or night. Other apps couldn’t do what you do and I’m so grateful. Thank you.

reviews.title: The Best App for Sleeping except…
reviews.text:
I have been a slumber user since the slumber app had its first sleep story. As someone with genetic chronic sleep issues, this app is a must. For anyone with sleep problems, slumber has guided me through nights of pain, extreme insomnia, and helped me with my lucid nightmares. I have PTSD, and this app has been genuinely indispensable. It is one of the best tools in my arsenal that I turn to, except for a few things that I consider brings this rating down. 

First, they use AI to generate their images for the backgrounds. As a professional artist this personally leaves a gross feeling for the app. I understand the high volume, but you could easily get a dedicated artist team to do photoshop to take this load away. This app makes money and has enough to keep paying its people and hire new voices and writers. The voices are legit people, and the stories are written by real people. But the art is not. It genuinely makes me use the app less because I see it and it’s obvious. 

Aside from this, the sorting in this app is awful. When they first added the search bar I tell you I was ELATED. However, now with the sheer volume of content, it is difficult to find the things you like even if you favorite them. If I don’t remember the name of the thing I want, I scroll endlessly and even with it in alphabetical (which it sometimes is not) it’s still incredibly difficult to find what you’re looking for. I suggest that they start breaking down the stories and the other tabs even further to help with this. Another thing is they have some stories linked so they have them together, like traveling stories for example. Or specifically train stories. Which helps. Making those types of things categories I feel would help more. 

Another thing, I know this would help me personally. It is just a suggestion. It’s practically the only thing that stops my use of slumber full time and makes me turn to other forms of content. I would like the ability to make playlists myself. And have them loop, but not just on one story. My issue is that I need to have things play as I sleep, the whole time, or with silence my chronic nightmares immediately start. I need something constantly playing, and for me that does not inhibit my sleep. I have done sleep studies and know this for a fact. My brain seems to understand if I loop a story more than twice, and if I do that 8 hours I’m kind of screwed. A playlist would genuinely, sincerely, help that. I could mix stories and meditations, it would be 8 or more hours and I would not just have to listen to their small collection of long stories. Which I have. And my brain gets use to them and I have to use other things outside of slumber. 

Basically, slumber is a good app. It has a ton of options, and is definitely worth it. I feel like it could be a great app if it addressed these things. It will still remain at the top of my list, and it is still a good tool in my arsenal. Thank you for reading.
